findings.title: New abstract method order() breaks all existing CryptoProvider implementers
findings.body: The PR adds `int order();` as a non-default method to the public SPI interface `CryptoProvider`. Any third-party or downstream implementation of this interface (custom crypto providers deployed with Keycloak or with client libraries depending on keycloak-common) will no longer compile against the new interface, and classes compiled against the old interface will fail at runtime with `AbstractMethodError` when `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` invokes `CryptoProvider::order` during provider sorting (CryptoIntegration.java line 57), which happens on every `CryptoIntegration.init` call. Since this is a public extension point, the method should have a default implementation (e.g. `default int order() { return 0; }`) to preserve source and binary compatibility.

findings.title: Equal-order providers are now selected non-deterministically and misconfiguration no longer fails fast
findings.body: The previous behavior threw an IllegalStateException when more than one CryptoProvider was found on the classpath, which protected against accidental misconfiguration. Now providers are silently sorted by `order()` and the first one wins. However, `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `FIPS1402Provider` and `WildFlyElytronProvider` all return order 200, so when two of them are present the winner is decided solely by ServiceLoader iteration order (i.e. classpath/jar ordering), which is not deterministic. Concretely, a FIPS deployment that accidentally also has the non-FIPS default provider module on the classpath can silently start using non-FIPS-validated crypto with only a debug-level log line ("Ignored crypto providers"), instead of the previous hard failure. Ties on order should either be rejected or at least logged at warn/error level.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the JVM default keystore provider, violating the interface contract
findings.body: `getBouncyCastleProvider()` is specified in `CryptoProvider` to return the BouncyCastle security provider, and callers in keycloak-common/core use it to obtain BC-specific algorithms (e.g. keystore types like BCFKS, PKCS7 ciphers). This implementation returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which on a stock JVM is the SUN provider. Any shared code path that reaches this method will get a provider that does not implement the BC algorithms the caller expects and fail in confusing ways (e.g. NoSuchAlgorithmException for BCFKS, or wrong padding behavior). Since the stated purpose of this provider is a minimal no-BC implementation where unsupported operations throw `UnsupportedOperationException`, this method should do the same rather than return an unrelated provider.

findings.title: Dead code in concatenatedRSToASN1DER creates and discards two ASN1Encoder instances
findings.body: Lines 114-115 (`ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger); ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);`) create two encoders, write the values into them and throw the results away; only the sequence built on lines 117-121 is returned. This is dead code left over from development that allocates objects for nothing and is confusing to readers. It should be removed.

findings.title: Test only checks round-trip, not that the converted DER signature is a valid ECDSA signature
findings.body: The test converts ASN.1 DER -> concatenated RS -> DER -> concatenated RS and asserts the two concatenated forms match. This would pass even if the DER re-encoding were wrong in a way that cancels out in the round-trip (e.g. incorrect minimal-encoding or sign handling in ASN1Encoder.write(BigInteger) producing invalid INTEGER encodings that the decoder mirrors). The test should verify the DER output with `Signature.initVerify(keyPair.getPublic())` (or compare `asn1Des` with the original `sign` bytes), and it should also cover edge cases such as r/s values with leading zero bytes or the high bit set. There is also no test that `CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader())` actually selects `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` via the new META-INF/services file and the ordering logic, which is the core mechanism introduced by this PR.
